title: Former UBS president: Biden likely to run, but I'll support Clinton
description: Fmr. UBS Americas President Robert Wolf explains why he doesn't believe there was a conflict of interest when Hillary Clinton helped the company avoid the IRS and also why he will back Hillary Clinton in the election. Watch Trish Regan talk about Opinion on Intel Trish Regan.

asr.full_text: Everyone says Americans. They are not so optimistic about this economy and they are not happy with the Obama recovery Less than half so they approve of the job this president is doing and that is not good news the Democrats on the campaign trial why Hillary Clinton here being forced to criticize our economy I've had the opportunity to listen To Americans concerns about an economy that still isn't delivering for them. It still seems to most Americans that I have spoken with that it is stacked for those at the top. Okay, of course, the Democrats have been in the White House for nearly seven years. They just haven't been able to fix the economy for whatever reason. For more on these electionomics issues, I am to ask you about UBS, the Clintons. Yeah. And the Clinton program. And what is it? We have a couple of people here who work very hard on this. But we are having a much more lively debate. I really do. Okay. So I was telling you last week, you'll be listening to the conversation, but you're going to get to the core theme of the election, which is what we call a clear election all right. We're gonna get to that. But I wanna ask you about UBS, the Clintons, and the IRS. So, you know, go back to Hillary Clinton as Secretary of State. You were then running UBS Americas and Bill Clinton was getting about one and a half million dollars in payouts from UBS for speaking engagements. At the same time, Hillary Clinton intervened on behalf of your bank to help out with some IRS inquiries. They were looking for roughly 52,000 people's information for tax evasion purposes and they wound up with $4400 that they had to give, so this was considered a bit of a win for UBS. And she helped you in all of this. Critics are saying it was a conflict of interest. What do you say? Because you were there at the bank at the time. Well, as you know, as I went through my presidential appointee vetting, I wasn't part of that. That was out of wealth management. And also the IRS was being handled out of Switzerland, not out of the U.S. I don't see the conflict. I think it was handled by a Department of Justice, not by the State Department. And with respect to Clinton Global Initiative, the things they're doing has been incredibly positive for the country and the globe. You can understand how people do see it as a conflict, right? Because especially when you look at the money that UBS gave to Clinton Global Initiative in that time period as well, increasing donations significantly. CONTINUE TO HAVE A CONFICIT AS INFLATION IN MENU. HOW COULD WE KEEP THE CONFLICT AS A COFFIN. ESPECIALLY WHEN YOU LOOK AT THE MONEY UBS GAVE TO CLINTON GLOBAL INITIATIVE. INCREASING DONATIONS SIGNIFICANTLY. I WASN'T AWARE AND I READ and ebola and all that has been fantastic, i'm a huge proponent So you never saw a conflict of interest there between Hillary Clinton secretary of state helping UBS out while at the same time they were donating to clinton global initiative and paying her husband? no, i think the secretary of state and the clinton global initiative were separated completely i don't think it was any conflict well one hope so because you're big democratic fundraiser you...are you supporting Hillary? I am any conflict. Well, one hopes so, because you're a big Democratic fundraiser. Are you supporting Hillary? I am. No interest in Joe Biden? No, of course, as a Democrat, we love Joe. He is a great vice president, and if he decides to run, people will have incredible excitement. He's got good favorability ratings. We were just talking about that. No question, I saw them. He has good favorability, but the Secretary was beating those people as well. I THINK IT'S GETTING FAVORABILITY RATINGS, HAD YOU HAD A GOOD FAVORABILITY, THE SECRETARY WAS BEATING THOSE PEOPLE AS WELL. I THINK POLL BASE FOR THE DAY BUT 16-MONTHS IS A LIFETIME, AS WE KNOW, TO ME IF JOE DECIDES TO RUN, YOU KNOW, HE'LL DECIDE THAT, NOBODY ELSE, I MEAN OBVIOUSLY WHAT HAPPENED WITH THE SON IS HEART WRENCHING BEING A FATHER OF BOYS AND SO, I THINK HE WILL HAVE TO MAKE UP HIS OWN MIND AND THERE WILL BE DEBATES AND REAL CAMPAIGNS... being a father of boys myself. And so I think he'll just have to make up his own mind and then there'll be real debates and a real campaign. Is there an over-under on it? I mean, what do you think, do you think he's gonna be in? I've already said, I think it's likely he'll be running. I mean, I think he's leaning that way, but certainly I don't know. And if that's the case? I've already said I don't know how many different ways I'll be supporting the secretary. Let's talk a little bit about the economy we've seen under President Obama. You said you took issue with what we said, what I said as we introduced this segment. Why? Because there's two questions. One, are we where we want to be? The answer is no. It's going to take time. We were in the deepest recession since the 40s. It's been seven plus years Robert. Well good. So let's talk about the facts of the seven plus years. I wrote some facts. Romney's goal was to get unemployment to below six percent in 2016. We just announced the last unemployment rate of 5.1 percent. We've had 8 million jobs over the last three years, fastest pace over a thirty six month period ever the unemployment rate has gone from ten percent to five percent 5.1 and more importantly for all your viewers the stock market is up more than double well I think if we talked about that and it ain't what it used to be Robert it really isn't I mean these jobs they're not paying well you look at the labor participation rate it hasn't been as bad since the nineteen seventies of one of the reasons why employment is so low no one's They're not paying well. You look at the labor participation rate. It hasn't been this bad since the 1970s. That's one of the reasons why unemployment is so low. No one's challenging that we want it to do better. I don't think that's the question. But the question I have, are we doing better? The answer is yes. It doesn't feel like it. I mean, you go out there to anyone in America. It sure doesn't feel like it. I'm with you. I think right now we don't see higher wages. I think that's a concern. I think if you look at some of the things were doing the lack of the EXIM bank reauthorisation that helps exports the lack of an infrastructure bank that the president actually is recommended which by the way is the fastest multiplier of GDP growth in jobs in the country. There are things that have been on the table that because a partisan politics, both sides, we've been able to get done And I think a lot of people blame President Obama WE ARE AT THE POINT EVERYBODY IS PROUD OF OUR LEADERSHIP. I THINK SO, SUCH AS OTHER LEADERS OF EVERY COUNTRY. THERE ARE THINGS THAT HAVE BEEN ON THE TABLE THAT PARTISAN POLITICS, BOTH SIDES, WE'VE BEEN ABLE TO GET DONE. I THINK A LOT OF PEOPLE BLAME PRESIDENT OBAMA FOR A LOT OF THAT. NOT SURPRISING THAT THE LEADER OF THE FREE WORLD GETS BLAMED. THAT'S NOT A CLASS TO ME. SO THIS IS SOMETHING THAT HEATHER CONTINUES TO BE LOOKING AT THE FACTS. HILLARY CLINTON OR JOAN BIDEN WILL HAVE TO OVERCOME. THE GOOD THING IS IT Clinton or Joe Biden will have to overcome. Well, the good thing is it will be one of them in the White House, and so we'll have another eight or nine years. I don't know. I don't know about that. It's going to be an interesting date. It will be. It's good to have you here. Good to see you. It's great to be here. Thank you for that great questioning as always. Sorry.
